candidates.lead: Conor Rand says Cresta Court Hotel in Altrincham will "end housing asylum seekers" within months
candidates.evidence_text: Altrincham hotel to stop housing asylum seekers, MP says - BBC News Image caption, Cresta Court Hotel in Altrincham has been used to house male asylum seekers since November 2024 By Kevin Fitzpatrick , Greater Manchester political reporter and Rachael Lazaro , North West Published 43 minutes ago A hotel that has been the scene of anti-immigration demonstrations and counter-protests over the last two years will stop housing asylum seekers, the local MP has said. Labour's Conor Rand confirmed the 148-bedroom Cresta Court in Altrincham, Greater Manchester, would "end housing asylum seekers within the next three months as the remaining residents are moved out of the hotel". The local Conservative group claimed the decision came off the back of its "two years of relentless campaigning". A spokesperson for the Home Office said the closure was part of its policy of "closing every asylum hotel and moving asylum seekers into alternative accommodation, including former military sites". Several protests have taken place outside Cresta Court since it began being used to house asylum seekers in 2024, attracting a large police presence. Image source, Reuters Image caption, Anti-immigration protesters gathered outside the hotel in August last year Rand told BBC Radio Manchester : "Hotels are not suitable places to house asylum seekers. "It's bad news for community, bad news for taxpayers, and bad news for people themselves seeking asylum. "It's a practice that should never have been started." Image caption, Labour MP Conor Rand says hotels are "not suitable" places to house asylum seekers In 2023, at the peak of the policy of housing asylum seekers in hotels, 400 were in use at a cost of £9m a day, according to the government. It said "fewer than 160 hotels remain in use today". In August, it was announced three north-west England hotels housing asylum seekers - the Metropole on Blackpool Promenade, Britannia Ashley Hotel in Hale, Altrincham, and Chimney House in Sandbach, Cheshire - had been handed back to their owners. But opposition parties have accused the government of just moving people elsewhere and not fixing the problem. The Home Office spokesperson said: "We are working to fairly house asylum seekers across the country while engaging closely with local authorities to minimise impacts on communities." candidates.summary: Residents who have been informed that their flats will be bulldozed say they will continue to "fight"

candidates.practical_angle: Есть новый городской контекст для Greater Manchester.
candidates.lead: Residents who have been informed that their flats will be bulldozed say they will continue to "fight"
candidates.evidence_text: Demolition of Rochdale's Seven Sisters flats devastating, residents say - BBC News Image caption, Christina Hartley and Roy Kitcher say the flats are "home" and they do not want to move By Davinia Ramos , Reporting from in Rochdale and Rebecca Brahde , North West Published 1 hour ago Residents of a town's tower blocks which are set to be demolished have said it is "devastating" but they will continue to "fight" the decision. Rochdale's Seven Sisters tower blocks, which contain 766 flats, will be replaced by about 600 homes , social landlord Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has said. Demolition of the tower blocks was first proposed in 2017 but was ruled out in 2023 after a local campaign against it, but residents began moving out in October 2025 over long-term safety concerns. Roy Kitcher and Christina Hartley, who have lived in one of the blocks for 14 years, said they were left "upset" and "angry". RBH said demolition was the only "realistic and affordable" option. Kitcher said: "It's devastating news - why they want to knock them down, I don't know." The couple are one of 78 households yet to accept an offer of another home. "This is home and I want to stay here, I don't want to be moving out again," Kitcher added. Hartley said: "I'm just so upset about it and angry." She said the council had asked her to look at accommodation, however it was not in the town. "I want to stay in Rochdale, I'm a Rochdale girl born and bred and I won't move until they find me somewhere round here," she said. Image source, Reuters Image caption, The seven sisters in Rochdale were built in the 1960s A local campaign, previously backed by Rochdale Council, had appealed for the buildings to be refurbished rather than demolished. But previous building surveys have identified structural and electrical issues with the tower blocks, as well as problems with water pumps and roof damage. RBH said refurbishment would have cost at least £269m and would have taken 12 years. Kitcher argued that the flats merely needed the heating and drafty doors and windows "sorting out." "They don't need to be taken back bare brick to be done up like they are saying, they just need to be liveable homes," he said. "I'm still going to fight them, to stop them the best way we can - I've got a meeting with two of the heads of Rochdale Council and I am going to push for them to do something to keep these flats up," he added. Image caption, Joan Wainwright, 72, moved into her flat when she was 36, and bought it ten years later Joan Wainwright who has lived at at Town Mill Brow for 36 years, said: "As far as I'm concerned I am too old. At 72 why should I have to go property hunting. "Thinking about selling all my furniture, which I'm not prepared to do, and starting all over again – no. "The square footage of these flats, as a two bedroom flat is bigger than a lot of terraced housing - so they have got to find us like for like." In a statement, MP for Rochdale Paul Waugh said it was a "sad day for College Bank and for Rochdale. "It's hard to ignore that a lack of investment over many years has contributed to where we are now, and residents have paid the price for that. "What matters now is that residents get certainty and a real say in what comes next," he said, adding that consultation needed to be "genuine" and include residents who had already moved out. "I also want the council and other providers involved in shaping the future of the site, so that it delivers the good-quality homes Rochdale needs," he added. RBH Chief Executive Amanda Newton said: "College Bank has been home to generations of Rochdalians, and we recognise the important place the blocks hold in many people's memories." She said replacing the buildings was the "only realistic and affordable way" to provide suitable homes for residents. "Our top priority is our customers, and our focus remains on supporting every remaining customer to find a home that is right for them," she added. candidates.evidence_text: A town's landmark tower blocks, which have dominated its skyline since the 1960s, are set to be demolished after years of uncertainty over their future Rochdale's Seven Sisters tower blocks, which contain 766 flats, will be replaced by about 600 homes, social landlord Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) said Residents began moving out of the flats in October 2025 following concerns about their long-term safety but a local campaign, previously backed by Rochdale Council, had appealed for the buildings to be refurbished rather than demolished But RBH said replacing the buildings was the "only realistic and affordable way" to provide suitable homes for residents Refurbishment would have cost at least £269m and would have taken 12 years, RBH said Some 78 households have yet to accept an offer of another home

candidates.lead: Hundreds of people were able to encounter their heritage first-hand at a church in Stockport
candidates.evidence_text: More than 400 Coptic Christians have had the rare opportunity to examine manuscripts which were centuries old - thanks to a library in Manchester People travelled from across the UK to read the manuscripts, which were written in Coptic - an ancient Egyptian language - with some dating back to the 10th century The historical Coptic and Ethiopian manuscripts are normally housed in The University of Manchester's John Rylands Library Dr Jeremy Penner, senior curator at the library, said there was "something quite remarkable" about a manuscript "finding itself once again among people who know its prayers, recognise its saints and continue its traditions" "These books may belong to the Rylands, but their stories belong to a much larger world," he said Among the manuscripts on display were biblical texts, Coptic liturgies and a Holy Week lectionary

The situation has now left the council with a toxic problem to deal with Town hall bosses are set to carry out ‘urgent’ works at Royton Library due to the need to tackle toxic asbestos. Asbestos is a fibrous mineral that was valued for its strength and fireproofing capabilities in old buildings and was widely used It is now banned from use, but if disturbed where it is still present, those fibres cause severe, incurable lung diseases. Around 5,000 people are estimated to die from asbestos-related issues every year The library was refurbished as part of a major £4m scheme which finished in 2024. However, earlier this year, the library had to shut suddenly and has remained closed since A council report said that in July 2026, library staff ‘reported that flooring in certain areas was becoming ‘bouncy’’ and ‘severe signs of dry rot’ were later discovered. Further investigations were carried out once the library closed

Abbas Hussain was sentenced to seven years' detention in a Young Offender Institution in April this year for manslaughter He stabbed Mohammed Isa Afzal, 19, to death with a 'Call of Duty-type' knife in the car park of a five-a-side football complex in Bury in the summer of 2025. Hussain was 19 at the time, and 20 when he was sentenced The incident took place at the Power League complex on Market Street in Bury town centre Hussain, of Windsor Crescent, Prestwich , was convicted of manslaughter after a trial at Manchester Crown Court . He was also found guilty of possession of an offensive weapon. He was found not guilty of a charge of murder The case was referred to the Attorney General’s Office for consideration, with the sentence subsequently referred up to the Court of Appeal by the office under the Unduly Lenient Sentence scheme

candidates.evidence_text: Altrincham Cresta Court Hotel in Altrincham to stop housing asylum seekers The hotel has been shut to public bookings in November 2024 Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 19:28, 16 Nov 2026 View Image Cresta Court Hotel (Image: Ge A second Altrincham hotel will soon stop housing asylum seekers, a local MP has announced In a post to Facebook today, Altrincham and Sale West MP Connor Rand said Cresta Court will be stood down as an asylum hotel by the Government. Those still living there will be leaving ‘over the next few months’ The hotel was shut to public bookings in November 2024. It's believed to have been home to around 300 asylum seekers The use of the hotel, along with the Britannia Ashley Hotel, in Hale , for this purpose has been a source of community tensions over the years. The two sites have seen protests from residents and groups and calls for them to be returned to community use Use of the Ashley Hotel for asylum seekers, which began in 2023, ceased in August

And that’s when I found out I really was the winner. I’ve never won anything before in my life!" View 3 Images Geoff and Lorraine (Image: Travelbag )

candidates.evidence_text: NHS Greater Manchester hospitals pay row escalates as more strikes announced More than 400 staff at four Greater Manchester hospitals will walk out again this week Add to preferred sources Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 19 More than 400 staff at four Greater Manchester hospitals will walk out again this week, with protests planned in the city centre as a long-running pay dispute escalates Trade union Unison has announced theatre staff at Salford Royal Hospital, Royal Oldham Hospital, Rochdale Infirmary and Bury ’s Fairfield Hospital will stage further strike action, starting from this Wednesday (November 18), when striking staff also plan to lobby health bosses be Theatre staff, including nurses, clinical support workers and housekeepers, at Northern Care Alliance (NCA) NHS Trust will then walk out again on Monday (November 23), Tuesday (November 24) and Friday (November 27) Striking staff will also protest in Manchester city centre next Friday, marching past Number 10 North before meeting local MPs at the Mechanics Institute, the union said The planned strikes will bring the total strike days since June to 21. The dispute centres around the use of outside agency NHS Professionals (NHSP) to manage additional shifts

The situation has now left the council with a toxic problem to deal with Town hall bosses are set to carry out ‘urgent’ works at Royton Library due to the need to tackle toxic asbestos. Asbestos is a fibrous mineral that was valued for its strength and fireproofing capabilities in old buildings and was widely used It is now banned from use, but if disturbed where it is still present, those fibres cause severe, incurable lung diseases. Around 5,000 people are estimated to die from asbestos-related issues every year The library was refurbished as part of a major £4m scheme which finished in 2024. However, earlier this year, the library had to shut suddenly and has remained closed since A council report said that in July 2026, library staff ‘reported that flooring in certain areas was becoming ‘bouncy’’ and ‘severe signs of dry rot’ were later discovered. Further investigations were carried out once the library closed

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan The railway bridge in Wigan named as one of Britain's 'most bashed' 'A bridge strike is never a minor incident' Add to preferred sources Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 17:46, 16 Nov 2026 View 2 Images Examples of bridge strikes (Image: Netw A railway bridge in Wigan has been named by Network Rail as one of the 'most bashed' in Britain. Rail chiefs have released a list of the top 10 locations of bridge strikes - with the structure on Prescott Street in Wigan coming in joint 10th position Network Rail said a staggering 1,706 bridge strikes were recorded in 2025/26, causing 185,319 minutes of delays and costing around £13.25m in delays, cancellations and repairs The Watling Street railway bridge on the A5 in Hinckley, Leicestershire, topped the 2025/26 list with 26 strikes, but there were 12 at Prescott Street in Wigan The statistics were revealed as the national Road Safety Week 2026 starts this week. Network Rail said the latest figures show that 1,706 bridge strikes were recorded between 1 April 2025 and 31 March 2026 – around one every five hours In December 2025, Network Rail began a three-month trial of new technology designed to support faster assessment of bridge strikes

Abbas Hussain was sentenced to seven years' detention in a Young Offender Institution in April this year for manslaughter He stabbed Mohammed Isa Afzal, 19, to death with a 'Call of Duty-type' knife in the car park of a five-a-side football complex in Bury in the summer of 2025. He was also found guilty of possession of an offensive weapon. He was found not guilty of a charge of murder The case was referred to the Attorney General’s Office for consideration, with the sentence subsequently referred up to the Court of Appeal by the office under the Unduly Lenient Sentence scheme

He set himself up as a hired gun when he struggled to make a living after being released from prison His low fees reflected his desperation - and the fact he wasn't very good at his job. The father-of-one had failed to kill one man and missed a second target altogether Tragically, the third job saw an innocent shopworker gunned down in a case that exposed a deadly gang rivalry in Oldham and Bolton Henderson's previous crimes included robbing a Post Office and stealing £40,000 of drugs money. candidates.evidence_text: Rochdale 'A sad day for College Bank and for Rochdale' as Seven Sisters tower blocks to be demolished After a decade of limbo for residents living in the iconic tower blocks - a decision on the future of the Seven Sisters has been made Add to preferre Residents of the Seven Sisters tower blocks in Rochdale have been left saddened, angered and disappointed after learning their homes are going to be bulldozed Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) have made the decision to demolish the 766 flats and replace them with a mix of 601 new flats and townhouses. The decision brings to an end an era of uncertainty for the towers, actually called College Bank, which were first earmarked for demoli What used to be a bustling community on the outskirts of Rochdale town centre now sits silent. That’s because only around 80 households remain from the original 766 since the original demolition announcement 10 years ago The uncertainty about the blocks' future has led many tenants to move on. Even hardened campaigners from the Save the Seven Sisters (ST7S) group have gone The campaigners have fought to stop demolition ever since it was first mentioned in 2016. They want to see the 1960s block refurbished instead

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Oldham library's bouncy floors and the toxic problem lurking underneath them The floors, which staff said became bouncy, reveals a toxic problem town hall bosses are now having to grapple with Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barne An Oldham library closed after staff discovered the floor was becoming ‘bouncy’. The situation has now left the council with a toxic problem to deal with Town hall bosses are set to carry out ‘urgent’ works at Royton Library due to the need to tackle toxic asbestos. Asbestos is a fibrous mineral that was valued for its strength and fireproofing capabilities in old buildings and was widely used It is now banned from use, but if disturbed where it is still present, those fibres cause severe, incurable lung diseases. Around 5,000 people are estimated to die from asbestos-related issues every year The library was refurbished as part of a major £4m scheme which finished in 2024. However, earlier this year, the library had to shut suddenly and has remained closed since A council report said that in July 2026, library staff ‘reported that flooring in certain areas was becoming ‘bouncy’’ and ‘severe signs of dry rot’ were later discovered. Further investigations were carried out once the library closed

candidates.evidence_text: The Met Office Greater Manchester hour-by-hour snow forecast as Met Office warning issued A yellow weather warning for snow comes into effect from midnight Add to preferred sources News Liv Clarke Tourism writer 17:09, 16 Nov 2026 Updated 18:16, 16 No A yellow weather warning for snow is in force for parts of the UK overnight, including Greater Manchester, from midnight until 11am on Tuesday. The alert covers North West England, South West Scotland and parts of Yorkshire, Derbyshire and the North East The Met Office warns that snow could cause travel disruption over higher ground early on Tuesday. Forecasters said a band of rain heading northwards across the UK overnight is likely to turn to snow for a time as it encounters cold air across the region covered by the warning This will mainly affect locations at 100-200m altitude or higher, with snow falling below this level “likely to be temporary and quickly melt.” Forecasters added that where snow does accumulate, depths of 1-5 cm are likely; and some locations above 300-400 m could see 5-15 cm It may result in travel disruption on higher level routes, the Met Office warns, particularly in combination with a strong easterly wind which could also cause localised drifting. There is also the risk that ice could impact infrastructure such as power lines, while snow turning View 2 Images A Met Office snow warning covers part of the region (Image: Met Office)

candidates.evidence_text: Stockport People left feeling threatened and intimidated as masked group march through Stockport The protest has been widely condemned. Stockport's council leader Coun Mark Roberts said: "We will not allow division to undermine the strong communities Stopfordians were left ‘feeling intimidated and threatened’ after balaclava-clad people marched through the town centre and ‘targeted’ public officials, an MP has said On November 15, people were seen marching through Stockport wearing balaclavas behind a banner appearing to protest houses of multiple occupation (HMOs) and asylum seekers . Photos of a number of Stockport councillors, a town hall officer, a community representative, and MP Naven HMOs are properties where at least three tenants live there, forming more than one household. They can provide a more affordable and flexible form of accommodation that are often used by young professionals and students However, HMOs have also become a national flashpoint as some of them have been used to house asylum seekers. Councils do not choose where and how asylum seekers are placed with decisions made by the UK Government’s Home Office and its contractors Coun Mark Roberts, Leader of Stockport Council , said: “Stockport is a proud, welcoming borough, built on strong communities, mutual respect and people looking out for one another

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan The railway bridge in Wigan named as one of Britain's 'most bashed' 'A bridge strike is never a minor incident' Add to preferred sources Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 17:46, 16 Nov 2026 View 2 Images Examples of bridge strikes (Image: Netw A railway bridge in Wigan has been named by Network Rail as one of the 'most bashed' in Britain. Rail chiefs have released a list of the top 10 locations of bridge strikes - with the structure on Prescott Street in Wigan coming in joint 10th position Network Rail said a staggering 1,706 bridge strikes were recorded in 2025/26, causing 185,319 minutes of delays and costing around £13.25m in delays, cancellations and repairs The Watling Street railway bridge on the A5 in Hinckley, Leicestershire, topped the 2025/26 list with 26 strikes, but there were 12 at Prescott Street in Wigan The statistics were revealed as the national Road Safety Week 2026 starts this week. Network Rail said the latest figures show that 1,706 bridge strikes were recorded between 1 April 2025 and 31 March 2026 – around one every five hours In December 2025, Network Rail began a three-month trial of new technology designed to support faster assessment of bridge strikes

Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

Credit: 499883 A man who murdered a mother and four of her children in a firebomb attack had been arrested and released by police despite Zak Bolland, 26, walked free from a police station after giving a 12-minute ‘no comment’ interview for breaking the windows of the home of Michelle Pearson, 37, and her young family in Jackson Street in Walkden, Greater Manchester on November 26 2017 Bolland’s previous convictions and suspended jail sentence he was serving at the time had not been checked by police and he was told he would be ‘NFA’d’ – no further action taken against him over the windows attack, Bolton Coroner’s Court heard Thirteen days later, in the dead of night on December 11 2017, he smashed Ms Pearson’s windows again and tossed in a petrol bomb which “exploded” near the stairs, blocking the only exit to the ground floor and trapping the victims upstairs Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, all died in the blaze Ms Pearson suffered 68% burns to her body and “clung on to life” until she died, 20 months after the attack on August 25 2019

candidates.evidence_text: A man who drugged and raped his wife for more than 20 years agreed it was "risky as hell, but the thought of it is so hot", a jury has heard The victim's husband, who cannot be identified to protect his wife's anonymity, pleaded guilty in September to offences from 2004 onwards - including rape, sexual assault and administering a substance with intent to commit a sexual offence He will give evidence later this month against nine men on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court Jurors have heard the husband took images and videos of his offending at the couple's home in Stockport, Greater Manchester, as she lay "out of it" on their bed, and then shared them online From 2023 onwards, the Crown said the husband had begun inviting other men to the address where it is said they sexually abused her On Monday, prosecutors read out an online conversation in December 2024 between the husband and an individual referred to as Contact BP

candidates.evidence_text: New plans to boost air quality across Manchester between now and 2040 are being brought forward by the Council Manchester’s air quality has improved significantly in recent years due to investment in public transport and cycling and walking routes, cleaner vehicle technology including electric vehicles and stricter national emissions standards. The investment-led Greater Manchester Clean But while good progress has been made, the Council wants to go further because environmental air pollution remains a real health risk, especially for people in more disadvantaged communities or with existing health conditions who can be more vulnerable to its effects The Vision is simple: “Manchester will be a city where everyone can breathe cleaner air and live healthier lives.” Alongside it sits a headline action plan which will guide further measures to improve air quality across the city, based around four priorities Reduce people’s exposure to air pollution, prioritising the most vulnerable such as children and people with existing health conditions and communities where the potential health benefits are the greatest

candidates.title: Saddleworth residents to vote on Neighbourhood Plan in December
candidates.summary: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026
candidates.reason: Visible repeat policy allows this item: publishable_anchor:new_phase. LLM-review: Заголовок идентичен, дата референдума 10 декабря уже была указана | Selection: Selected in city_watch shortlist before writing.

candidates.lead: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026
candidates.evidence_text: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026 The referendum will ask residents whether they want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan to help decide planning applications in the area The plan sets out local planning policies for Saddleworth and, if approved, will become part of the area’s statutory Development Plan, helping to guide decisions on future planning applications Residents will be asked the following question “Do you want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Neighbourhood Plan for Saddleworth to help it decide planning applications in the neighbourhood area?” To vote, residents must be registered to vote in local government elections and have a qualifying address within the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Area

candidates.title: Oldham to light up with spectacular free programme of events for Autumn/Winter 2026
candidates.summary: From the fabulous Feast of Fire celebrations to the iconic Christmas Lights Switch-On, the town centre will host an exciting calendar of entertainment as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture 2026
candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Validator: news item is 34 days old (hard cutoff 14d), dropped regardless of update wording.

candidates.lead: From the fabulous Feast of Fire celebrations to the iconic Christmas Lights Switch-On, the town centre will host an exciting calendar of entertainment as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture 2026
candidates.evidence_text: From the fabulous Feast of Fire celebrations to the iconic Christmas Lights Switch-On, the town centre will host an exciting calendar of entertainment as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture 2026 The programme will showcase the very best of Oldham's culture, creativity and community spirit with a series of free family-friendly events The programme begins with the Feast of Fire event on Saturday 31 October 2026. A joint celebration of Halloween and Bonfire Night, this spellbinding event will light up the heart of the town centre with fire dance performances and The Lips Halloween Show by Puppets with Guts foll Then, just two weeks later, the festive season will officially begin with the Oldham Christmas Lights Switch-On event on Saturday 14 November, starting from 1pm. The day will feature meet and greets with Peppa Pig, appearances from Oldham's mascots and activities by the Spindles The celebrations will continue into the evening with the big Switch On Show from 5.30pm featuring Father Christmas, Peppa Pig's Dance Party, Oldham Rock Choir and performances from Fierce Dance The Mayor of Oldham Cllr Pam Byrne will also take part in the celebrations before a local school child competition winner will switch on the town's Christmas lights. The evening will conclude with a festive fireworks finale, accompanied by a lights and laser show

candidates.evidence_text: Pupils across Bolton returning from the summer holidays last month were greeted by safer and warmer classrooms after the council invested in the borough’s schools Working with local employers Seddon, the council oversaw repairs and improvements at more than half a dozen schools, benefitting over 3,000 pupils from primary to secondary age The wide-ranging work was carried out over the summer break to minimise disruption The project saw some schools receiving new boilers and water heaters, new roof installed at one primary school, while another had more energy efficient windows installed Some fire alarm systems and emergency lighting have also been upgraded It is the second school decarbonisation project Seddon has delivered with Bolton Council, helping to improve the efficiency and long-term sustainability of school buildings across the borough

candidates.evidence_text: Alfie and family with Wigan Council and Bethell representatives at the Wigan Road crossing An eleven-year-old boy concerned about the safety of a busy main road has seen his request for a pedestrian crossing become a reality A frequent visitor to Ashfield Park in Standish, Alfie Haywood grew increasingly concerned about crossing Wigan Road to access the park, particularly when he was on his way home from school or crossing with his family and younger sister Encouraged by his nan Ruth, Alfie wrote a letter to Wigan Council and Lisa Nandy MP to raise his concerns and request a safer crossing, resulting in a toucan crossing being installed, along with improved road infrastructure for motorists, pedestrians, and cyclists Alfie, a pupil at St Peter’s High School in Orrell, said: “The reason I wanted this crossing is because lots of children and families visit Ashfield Park, but because this is such a busy road, somebody might get run over and hurt, and a crossing will allow people to cross the roa “I feel very proud and confident that the council listened to my idea, and I would like other children to know that they can help their community to become a better place

candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

candidates.lead: History, power and empire collide in Button Up!
candidates.evidence_text: History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humani Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . candidates.evidence_text: Cheers to the women who changed the way we drink! Hear the hidden history of the female pioneers who drank, distilled, and defied , while enjoying cocktails inspired by them Drinking history expert Simon Sharp takes you on a journey from the invention of the pub and modern beer, to distillation and champagne – where women have been at the forefront , challenging patriarchy so we can all enjoy a drink To illustrate these stories guests will enjoy four cocktails; The Mansplainer, The Poinsettia, Bees Knees, and Hanky Panky – all invented or inspired by these trailblazing ladies, crafted with ingredients sourced from female founded and led businesses A tribute to women’s creativity and courage , this tasting celebrates the mark they’ve left on drinking culture Simon Sharp is a history geek, drinks expert, and spirits judge. He travels around the country hosting tastings and talks revolving around the history of drinking. candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. Born in London into a Gambian griot lineage of seven centuries, she began learning the kora at age three with her brother Tunde Jegede and father Sanjally Jobarteh; her cousin was the late Toumani Diabaté. She studied at the Royal College of Music, the Purcell School of Music and SOAS University of London. In 2015 she founded The Gambia Academy, which puts African history and culture at the centre of its curriculum, and she has keynoted forums hosted by the UN and the World Trade Organization. In 2023 Berklee College of Music awarded her an honorary Doctorate in Music alongside Usher and Roberta Flack

candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

candidates.evidence_text: Counter Manchester , the much-anticipated new restaurant from Open Restaurant Group , opens its doors today at 12pm. It is the group’s first opening in Manchester city centre and brings a theatrical approach to dining to the heart of the city Led by acclaimed chef Andrew Sheridan, Counter is located in Manchester’s Island Building on John Dalton Street and has 60 covers. It is Open Restaurant Group’s ninth restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Didsbury in Sep At the focus of the restaurant is a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, which places guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. The interiors feature four-metre elm trees, curved booth seating and a brass wine display, so the atmosphere and experienc Award-winning Andrew Sheridan brings his internationally inspired approach to Counter, building on a career that has seen multiple restaurants under his direction feature in the prestigious Michelin Guide. At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot and From the grill, guests can enjoy the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallot, alongside the slow-cooked Thai Lamb Shoulder, served with red thai sauce, chilli and coriander

Cadno Lounge, Neath . Loungers, the West Country‑based café‑bar group, will open Fosforo Lounge, King Street in Stretford on Saturday 28th November 2026, creating around 30 new jobs for local people.. . Fosforo Lounge will be open all day, every day, serving breakfast, brunch, lunch, dinner and drinks, with dedicated kids’, gluten‑free and vegan menus. . The site on King Street has been transformed by the Loungers design team into a warm, eclectic ‘home from home’ – their signature style. Fosforo translates to matchstick and is a nod to Manchester-based painter LS Lowry’s ‘matchstick men’ style.. . Fosforo Lounge’s all‑day menu will cater for every taste, from hearty comfort food to healthier choices and indulgent treats. Families are a major focus, with games, books, colouring materials, high chairs and baby‑changing facilities available for Little Loungers.. . With community at its heart, Fosforo Lounge will offer a welcoming space for regular meet‑ups, business catch‑ups, book clubs, knitting groups, parent‑and‑baby sessions, creative workshops and more. Local groups looking for a friendly, flexible venue will be encouraged to get in touch.. . Vix Connolly, General Manager, Fosforo Lounge said: “We’re so looking forward to welcoming everyone to Fosforo Lounge on the 28th November. Becoming a genuine part of the community is incredibly important to us, and we can’t wait to meet our neighbours and get involved locally.. . “If you’re looking for a friendly, flexible space for events or group meet‑ups, pop in once we’re open – we’d love to chat and see how we can help.”. . . . . . . The group’s approach centres on cooking over fire, carefully-sourced ingredients, expertly-pr Sam Elliott, Chef-Owner of Pasture, commented: “Manchester is a city with a huge personality, a strong independent spirit and a real passion for great food, so bringing Pasture here is incredibly exciting. St Michael’s gives us the opportunity to create something that goes beyond “From our signature open-fire cooking at Pasture Manchester and Mediterranean-inspired all-day dining at Terrace, to the atmosphere of W Lounge and the much-loved character of the Abercromby, we’re looking forward to becoming part of the city’s dynamic hospitality scene.”

candidates.lead: Posted by Manchester Digital Introducing The Inside Track: A new way to get more from your Manchester Digital membership
candidates.evidence_text: Stay connected. Know what's next. We're launching The Inside Track , a new monthly online session designed to help Manchester Digital members stay informed, discover new opportunities and make the most of their membership Whether you've recently joined Manchester Digital or have been part of our community for years, The Inside Track is your chance to catch up with our team, find out what's happening across the network and explore ways to get more involved Taking place on the last Wednesday of each month, these free, members-only sessions will bring you up to speed on the latest developments, events and opportunities across Manchester Digital, all in just 30 minutes Each session will feature a topical focus, alongside practical updates on upcoming events, programmes, speaking opportunities and ways to raise your business's profile There'll also be time to ask questions, share your priorities and find out how we can help you get more value from your membership Our first edition at midday on 25th November will focus on some of the biggest opportunities coming up across the Manchester Digital community

candidates.evidence_text: Five days. Five themes. One city shaping its digital future. The first Manchester Digital Festival takes place from 8–12 February 2027 with its biggest and boldest programme yet. Manchester Digital has unveiled the programme for Manchester Digital Festival 2027 (MDF27 ) , bringin Taking place from Monday 8 to Friday 12 February 2027 , the festival marks an exciting new chapter for Manchester Digital, building on the success of Digital Skills Festival and expanding its scope to celebrate the full breadth of Greater Manchester's digital and technology secto The launch also comes as Manchester Digital celebrates its 25th anniversary , providing an opportunity to reflect on the people, businesses and innovations that have shaped the region's tech ecosystem, while looking ahead to what comes next With 15 events already announced and more to come, the first wave of the MDF27 programme offers everything from industry conferences and leadership discussions to careers events, founder stories and opportunities to explore emerging technologies Tickets for most events are now available , with further announcements expected in the coming months Under the banner Building our digital tomorrow , MDF27 introduces a new five-day format, with each day dedicated to a different theme reflecting the opportunities and challenges facing Greater Manchester's digital and technology sector

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

candidates.evidence_text: POWWR strengthens team with double appointment | Bdaily Joe Hemmings, left, and Ryan Ansell, who have joined POWWR POWWR strengthens team with double appointment Manchester-based energy software provider POWWR has strengthened its business development team with two appointments as it continues to expand. Ryan Ansell and Joe Hemmings join as SME business development managers, supporting the company’s growing network of energy brokers. Ryan brings 14 years’ experience in the energy industry, having previously held account management and relationship management roles at Online Direct. In his new position, he will focus on strengthening existing broker partnerships and developing new relationships to support business growth. Ryan said: “POWWR’s positive culture throughout the business really stood out to me. “All members of staff have been very welcoming and supportive. “I am excited to join the team at such a pivotal time and looking forward to leveraging my experience to help drive growth and add value to POWWR’s existing clients.” Joe also joins from Online Direct, where he spent four years as an account manager, having previously worked in the metering team at Opus. His role will involve working directly with brokers, building relationships and gathering feedback to support POWWR’s product development. Joe added: “I’m really excited and honoured to join POWWR at such a great time for the business. “Although I mainly work remotely, the company does a great job at keeping everyone well connected. “I have enjoyed my time out on the road, introducing myself to brokers, meeting them face-to-face and developing deeper relationships.” Their appointments follow a period of growth for the company, which has increased its headcount by 20 per cent since Paul Hodnett became chief executive earlier this year, following investment from Five Elms Capital. Paul added: “We are thrilled to welcome Ansell and Hemmings to our growing team. “What makes POWWR such a force in the industry is the people we have working for us. “I have no doubt that Ansell and Hemmings will help the brokers we work with win more deals and grow their businesses.” Want your business, product or service to be seen regionally and nationally? candidates.evidence_text: Legal AI leader Clio expands global footprint in Salford - Invest Manchester Skip to main content Skip to footer Opens in a new tab Digital, cyber & AI , Financial, professional, business services Legal AI leader Clio expands global footprint in Salford Published on November 11, 2026 News Clio , the global leader in legal AI, expands its UK presence with a move to Eden , having signed a deal with ECF to take the first fitted and furnished suite in Manchester’s highly sustainable, 12-storey workplace in New Bailey . Moving from Alderley Edge, Clio’s new 5,134 sq. ft office is a turnkey space designed for high-growth businesses, with 50 fixed workstations, dedicated pods and booths for focused work, board and meeting rooms, a kitchen complete with a dining area, and flexible touchdown spaces built to support collaboration. Already home to law firm TLT, accountancy and business advisory firm BDO, and the PE-backed professional services group Leonard Curtis, Eden offers move-in-ready office space designed to make taking on a new workspace simpler and more straightforward. Delivered by ECF, our partnership with Homes England’s National Housing Bank, L&G and Muse , the turnkey model streamlined Clio’s move into its new space, reducing the time and complexity typically associated with a traditional office fit-out. Moving into a city centre location brings Clio closer to its growing UK customer base following its recent acquisition of Manchester-based ShareDo, now Clio Operate , the legal work management platform for large firms and enterprise legal teams. Eden’s central location and modern amenities also support Clio’s continued growth by strengthening its ability to attract and retain talent. Following the successful letting of its first fitted and furnished workspace, ECF is now underway with two additional suites within Eden, delivered to a similar specification. The first of the two new suites will be available from December 2026, with the second scheduled to be available from early 2027. This will include a 4,886 sq. ft office on the same floor as Clio, and a 10,000 sq ft. space on the second floor, with ECF responding to continued demand for turnkey solutions of this nature across the sector. Organisations that move to Eden send a clear message that they’re committed to fostering a healthy, connected and collaborative workforce centred around wellness and wellbeing, along with demonstrating their ambition to create a sustainable future. Eden itself is home to a range of amenities, including on-site café, Spice & Grind, a yoga/contemplation studio, and a roof terrace, each designed to offer occupants space to take a break from day-to-day work schedules. Elsewhere there are enhanced fresh air rates which boost cognitive function; there’s an emphasis on natural light and planting to provide a connection to nature; and the whole building embraces the WELL Building Standard Principles to create a workplace that supports productivity and collaboration. In-keeping with Eden’s green credentials – which include being net zero carbon in operation – the new fitted and furnished suite has been designed with sustainability at its heart too, enabling the space to become the first fit-out in the UK to achieve both SKA V2 Gold certification and a Net Zero Aligned approach. This is in part thanks to a range of specific fixtures and furnishings which have been prioritised to incorporate high levels of circularity. This includes the use of cork for its renewable and recyclable properties, utilisation of 100% of the CAT A lighting, and the specification of recycled denim for elements of the kitchen chairs. Eden’s sustainability credentials and its focus on employee wellbeing were significant factors in Clio’s decision. Laura Percy, development director, said : “Welcoming Clio to Eden’s first fitted and furnished suite represents another significant staging post in this remarkable building’s journey, and we’re delighted to support Clio’s growth as it takes this next step. “Being part of Eden offers a working experience unlike any other, with a strong focus on connectivity, collaboration, wellbeing and sustainability. It is the ideal place for businesses looking to build a brighter future for both the company and its team. “Since its completion in 2024 Eden has become a Manchester landmark, with a green wall façade adorned with 350,000 plants. candidates.evidence_text: Iconic Manchester artist Stanley Chow has joined forces with Desperados to turn the city into one giant round of Lotería, with six oversized playing cards hidden across some of the city’s best-known cultural hotspots The collaboration sees the celebrated illustrator put his distinctive spin on the traditional Mexican card game, creating a series of bespoke designs which have been dotted around central Manchester as part of a seasonal treasure hunt Known for his pared-back, geometric portraits of musicians, politicians and pop culture figures, Chow has previously immortalised the likes of Liam Gallagher and Andy Burnham. For this latest project, his illustrations offer a fresh visual take on six classic Lotería characters: Each design has been matched with a Manchester location reflecting its subject and the city’s wider artistic, musical and cultural heritage, with cryptic clues providing the route between them Those keen to take part can follow the clues as they appear on Desperados’ Instagram account, collecting photographic evidence of all six cards before sending their finds to @desperados_uk via direct message. Completing the set enters participants into a prize draw, with three al The collaboration will extend beyond the hunt itself, with Desperados bringing Chow’s designs to a series of live events across the North this November. Manchester’s instalment takes place at YES on Thu 19 Nov, featuring a DJ set from record producer Conducta

It boasts gorgeous historic buildings alongside a whole network of trendy, independent hospitality and retail businesses. And it Hidden beneath the surface of all this are stories. This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

The title is the Latin plural of “asylum”, which can mean both a place of refuge and an institution for the insane – and the piece plays on this plurality. Its third movement, Ecstasio , is s Between these two pieces comes a world premiere: Gabriella Smith’s How To Be A Bird , written for tonight’s soloist Pekka Kuusisto. Hailed by the LA Times as “an outright sensation”, Smith writes music drawn from field recordings and underwater microphones, looking for what she c The evening closes with Stravinsky’s Firebird Suite , one of the happiest accidents in musical history. Sergei Diaghilev, head of the Ballets Russes, saw his first three choices to score a new ballet fall through before he gambled on an unproven 27-year-old; Stravinsky himself la Four works, then, that each began as a risk on someone (to varying degrees) untested – Stravinsky in 1910, Adès in 1996, Smith tonight. If this is Adès’s opening statement as Principal Guest Conductor, it’s a heartening one: a little faith in emerging composers can go a long way

candidates.evidence_text: Football Mauricio Pochettino Mauricio Pochettino 'begins Man United job early' as staff fly into UK to work Mauricio Pochettino is not expected to take the reins of Manchester United until later this week, but his staff are making a head start at Old Trafford Add to preferr Mauricio Pochettino's backroom staff have already arrived at Manchester United , as they look to pick up the pieces of a torrid start to the Premier League season. That's despite the Argentine head coach not arriving at Old Trafford until later this week The 54-year-old is committed to navigating a CONCACAF quarter-final double header with the United States national team before starting the next chapter of his career at the Theatre of Dreams. The Stars and Bars enjoyed a 6-0 rout of their Caribbean neighbours on Saturday in Miami As a result, Pochettino will not touch down on UK soil until the dust settles on that encounter. However, with the deficit being so big, the head coach has allowed his backroom staff to fly into Greater Manchester early to prepare for his arrival Jesus Perez, Toni Jimenez and Sebastian Pochettino - who is the son of Mauricio - flew into the north west on Saturday. While Miguel D'Adostino has remained Stateside with Pochettino, he is also expected to join the head coach when he officially takes up tenure with United on Nov It comes as Pochettino has his work cut out for him should he harbour any ambitions of turning the tide with the Reds. At the time of writing, the club sits 18th in the Premier League standings on eight points, having won just one of their opening 10 matches

The former Manchester City boss is believed to be at the top of US Soccer's wishlist after Pochettino's decision to take charge at Manche However, Guardiola is likely to turn down any approach to replace the Argentine as he is determined to take a year out of the game following his decade at City, reports the Telegraph. That is despite his obvious affection for the US, where he spent a previous sabbatical from mana It is no secret that Guardiola fancies a crack at international management one day. Last year, he said: "I would love to be in a World Cup, in a Euro, a Copa America [as a manager] He recently held talks about taking the Italy job, which went to Roberto Mancini, while he has previously been linked with the Brazil job, currently held by Carlo Ancelotti Get all the best Man City news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the MEN!
